text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

<final_document>
**Subject:** About last summer, and what we've changed

Hi [Name],

You didn't renew your share this year, and I suspect last summer had something to do with it.

When hail destroyed about half our crops on July 9, your boxes held about half the usual amount for six weeks. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent only one short email about it. You deserved a better explanation than that, and I'm sorry.

Here's what we've changed since then:

- **A second field on higher ground**, so one storm is less likely to hit everything we grow.
- **Two hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers.** The new field and the nets together cost $31,000.
- **Paid pauses:** you can now pause up to two weeks and get credit for them.

The price hasn't changed. A full share is still $540 for 22 weeks of Thursday pickups.

We have 52 shares left, and sign-up closes March 15. If you'd like to come back, you can sign up here: [link]

If you have questions, or want to tell me what last season was like for you, just reply. I read every reply.

Thanks for the seasons you spent with us.

[Your name]
[Farm name]
</final_document>

The email is about 190 words. I left out the 260 and 97 numbers because they're about your farm, not about the reader. The apology covers how you communicated about the hail, not the hail itself, and the email doesn't promise refunds or credit for last year. If you plan to offer either one, you'd need to add it.
